claims.item_en: Remove the first defendant from the management of the company
Annul the general assembly resolution of 30 Sep 2026 discharging the manager
Appoint an accounting expert to examine the company's accounts for 2025 and 2026
Manager to pay the company, provisionally, with the right to amend after the expert's report
Court fees, costs and lawyer's fees

key_facts.fact_en: Capital AED 300,000 in 300 shares: the manager 135 (45%), the claimant 120 (40%), Salma Rashid Al Naqbi 45 (15%)

The auditor refused to sign the 2025 accounts because AED 1,284,600 is unsupported: cash withdrawals of AED 418,500 without vouchers, AED 596,000 paid to Al Daffa Al Sharqiya Transport without a contract or original invoices, and an unexplained stock shortfall of AED 270,100
The company received the auditor's letter on 17 Sep 2026, 13 days before the general assembly; at the meeting the auditor was absent and the manager said the audit report was 'being issued'

Resolutions 2 to 4 (approving the accounts, discharging the manager, replacing the auditor) passed by 60%, the votes of the manager (45%) and Salma Rashid Al Naqbi (15%), against the claimant's 40%; the manager voted on his own discharge
The claimant signed the minutes with a handwritten objection to resolutions 2, 3 and 4: the accounts are unaudited, and the manager may not vote on his own discharge
Resolution 4 replaces the auditor and leaves the choice of the new auditor and the fee to the manager
The manager did not answer the claimant's request of 5 Oct 2026 to inspect the books

reader_should_flag: Article 380 of the Commercial Companies Law does not exist (the law ends at Article 365). It is cited clause first, as clause (2) of Article (380), as the basis for a partner's right to an expert at the company's expense.

The date the company received the auditor's letter (17 Sep 2026) appears only in the incoming-mail stamp on page 3. The claim relies on it ('about two weeks before the general assembly') without giving the date.
The claimant's objection on the minutes is handwritten only; the printed minutes record his votes against but not his reasons.
The manager voted his own 45% on his discharge (resolution 3), which Article 99 forbids; without his shares only 15% approved against 40%.
The accounts approved on 30 Sep 2026 were unaudited: the auditor had refused to sign them on 15 Sep 2026, yet the minutes record the manager saying the report was 'being issued'.
The draft 2025 accounts reached the auditor only on 11 May 2026, after the three-month limit in Article 87 (31 Mar 2026).
Resolution 4 replaces the auditor who refused to sign and leaves the choice of the new auditor and the fee to the manager, although under Article 102 the general assembly appoints the auditor.
